reviewConclusions: Source review progress derives from current source-scoped claims and the same canonical predicate as Added to My Care; no persisted source, original binary evidence, claim state, audit history, or model configuration is rewritten.

Failed, cancelled, interrupted, saved and edited-evidence recovery messages remain visible; successful analysis counts are replaced while analysis-limit and unsupported-FHIR disclosures are preserved.

Audio activation and release are serialized off the UI thread; obsolete activation, dismissal, cancellation, recording resume and delegate callbacks cannot start or stop a replacement run through the reviewed ownership guards.
Read-aloud cancellation and scene/session changes stop the owned speech request, and failure messages remain fixed recovery text rather than underlying audio errors.

Accessibility companion helper requires a complete visible native hit region; Loop helper moves the existing bounded stable-frame wait before its immediate hit assertion. Neither helper bypasses persistence or keyboard assertions.

BackupView Done only clears FocusState; there is no observer or task that deliberately forces SecureField focus back on. The remaining observed keyboard assertion failure has no production cause established from this source review.

limitations: This audit did not build, run simulators, mutate services, read credentials, or make paid API requests.
No claim that the complete final UI action passed: two actual case failures remain independently recorded; subsequent focused results must remain separately scoped.
Physical microphone, speaker, Bluetooth, native speech-recognition permissions and real hardware audio interruptions remain untested by injected simulator regressions.
Invalid-frame runtime warnings from earlier UI actions do not provide a symbolized app call stack; no ungrounded geometry repair or benign attribution is justified.
Pattern scanning and OCR cannot prove the absence of all possible secrets in binary/image artifacts.
App Store organization approval, signing/distribution identity and publication remain parent-owned release dependencies.
